blogs.title: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) — An Intuitive Guide for ML Practitioners
blogs.description: A friendly, nontechnical walkthrough of the DPO idea: why we can treat a language model as an implicit reward model, how the Bradley–Terry reparameterization works at a high level, and what this means for replacing RLHF with a simple classification loss. Includes visual explanations, toy examples, and when DPO is (and isn’t) appropriate.

blogs.title: Hands-on DPO: Implementing Direct Preference Optimization with Hugging Face and PyTorch
blogs.description: A practical tutorial that steps through a full DPO implementation: preparing preference datasets, initializing the reference model, coding the DPO loss, training loops, and evaluation. Includes ready-to-run code snippets, tips for batching/sequence-level log-probabilities, and advice on choosing beta and other hyperparameters.

blogs.title: DPO vs PPO vs Preferred-FT: Which Alignment Method Should You Use?
blogs.description: A comparative post that draws on the paper’s experiments and practical experience to explain strengths and weaknesses of DPO, PPO-based RLHF, supervised finetuning on preferred responses, unlikelihood training, and Best-of-N. Covers metrics to compare (reward vs KL, win-rate), compute and stability considerations, and recommended choices for common use cases.

blogs.title: Collecting and Curating Preference Data for DPO: Best Practices and Annotation Rubrics
blogs.description: Guidance for practitioners and students on how to collect reliable pairwise preference data suitable for DPO. Topics include prompt sampling strategies, annotation UI and rubrics, bias mitigation, synthetic labeling (LLM-in-the-loop), dataset balancing, and how to adapt existing public preference datasets for DPO training.

blogs.title: Understanding Beta and Model Conservatism: Tuning the KL Trade-off in DPO
blogs.description: A focused guide on the role of the beta parameter in DPO, how it shapes the implicit reward, and practical recipes to tune it. Contains diagnostic experiments to visualize the reward–KL frontier, rules of thumb for different tasks (sentiment control, summarization, chat), and pitfalls like model degeneration or over-optimization.

blogs.title: Failure Modes and Debugging DPO: From Degeneration to Reward Hacking
blogs.description: A troubleshooting post that catalogs failure modes observed when optimizing with DPO—probability collapse, overfitting to annotator quirks, undesirable shortcut behaviors—and gives concrete debugging steps: monitoring implicit reward ordering, sanity checks, regularization, dataset augmentation, and fallbacks to hybrid training strategies.

blogs.title: Scaling DPO: From 6B Models to Production-Scale LLMs
blogs.description: A pragmatic exploration of engineering and research questions for scaling DPO to very large models: memory-efficient training, offloading log-prob computation, distributed training recipes, inference-time sampling strategies, and how DPO’s simpler pipeline affects iteration speed and cost compared to RLHF.

blogs.title: From Preferences to Rewards (and Back): The Theory Behind DPO and Reward Equivalence
blogs.description: A deeper theoretical post for students and researchers that unpacks the reward-equivalence class idea, why the partition function cancels in Bradley–Terry, formal connections to control-as-inference, and implications for identifiability and generalization. Includes derivations, theorems in plain language, and open theoretical questions.

blogs.title: Beyond Text: Applying DPO to Multimodal and Non-Language Generative Models
blogs.description: An exploratory piece discussing how the DPO approach could transfer to other generative tasks (images, audio, robotics policies) that use pairwise preferences. Covers what changes (modeling choices, reference distributions, evaluation), potential benefits, and early experimental ideas or toy projects to try.
